zuexact

zuexact computes sums of doubles exactly and rounds once, at the end. The result is the correctly rounded true sum. It does not depend on the order of the elements, on the platform, or on how R was built. It is built on Radford Neal’s xsum superaccumulators.

Base R’s sum() accumulates in long double. That is 80-bit on x86-64 Linux and Windows, but the same as double on Apple Silicon and on R built without long doubles. So the same call gives different answers on different machines:

sum(c(1e16, 1, -1e16))
#> 1 on x86-64 Linux and Windows
#> 0 on Apple Silicon

The exact answer is 1, everywhere. zuexact’s xsum() will return it on every platform.

Status: under development; nothing is implemented yet. The design is in .agents/design.md and the plan to the first CRAN release in .agents/roadmap.md.

Installation

You can install the development version of zuexact from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zuexact")
